Overview
R414b is a multi-component refrigerant blend consisting of R-22, R-124, R-142b, and a small amount of hydrocarbon R-600a (isobutane) to improve mineral oil miscibility
. It is formulated to match the pressure and capacity of R12 systems, making it suitable for retrofitting automotive air conditioning and stationary refrigeration systems.

Straight tinwork, clean example. Wide front axle. Open station.

The flywheel design minimizes noise while maximizing a smooth feel.

title: Korg Kross 2 88 - Like New
ai_notes: [Korg Kross 2 88-key workstation] Popular workstation keyboard in good condition.
description:
Up for sale is my Korg Kross 2 88 key workstation.  Excellent condition, never gigged, never left my smoke-free home.  It's an excellent keyboard/synth/workstation, too many features to cover in this ad.  I'm selling it because I'm not using it enough.  I already own a Nautilus 76, and wanted to add a full size weighted hammer action piano to the mix.  But it turns out there are not that many songs we do that require it.  Also, it is more to carry and requires more space, and a lot of the places we play just don't have enough space on the stage to accommodate the larger stand and wider keybed.
I'm including some additional detail, but lots of articles and videos on YouTube if you are curious.
Priced to sell - asking half what it costs new.  I'm selling local first to avoid shipping, but if I don't sell soon it will be going to Reverb for a higher price.
Description
Korg's Kross 2 88-key synthesizer workstation is the only instrument a musician needs. Packed with over 1,000 top-tier sounds and a full suite of production tools, the Kross 2 delivers an unparalleled creative experience for composing, performing and everything in between. At the heart of this powerhouse workstation is the EDS-i sound engine, distilled from Korg's most advanced pro-level synths and loaded with 134 high-definition effects. The 88-key keybed features Korg's acclaimed NH (Natural Weighted Hammer Action) mechanism, giving piano and electric piano sounds a realistic, responsive feel.
Over 1,000 Sounds Cover All Musical Genres
The Kross 2 is armed with a massive collection of lavishly-sampled sounds taken from Korg's flagship workstations, providing a sonic spectrum far beyond its class. Grand piano decays are sampled at three velocity levels, capturing damper pedal resonances and other nuances for ultimate realism. From essential keyboards and drums to cutting-edge electronica, no genre is left out. Finding the right sound is effortless thanks to the intuitive sound selector and favorites function.
EDS-i Sound Engine Powers 134 Pro-Grade Effects
At the core of the Kross 2 is Korg's EDS-i sound engine, providing a studio-grade foundation for your music. EDS-i lets you use up to seven effects at once, including essentials like delay, reverb and chorus as well as amp modeling and a robot vocoder effect. Korg's REMS modeling technology ensures amp simulations sound rich, natural and dynamically responsive. With 134 high-quality effects on tap, you have all the tools to craft your signature sound.
Full Production Suite for Composing and Performing
The Kross 2 doesn't just play sounds--it's designed to help you create music. A 16-track MIDI sequencer, drum track, arpeggiator and step sequencer derived from Korg's Electribe grooveboxes provide an intuitive, hands-on environment for songwriting and beatmaking. Mic and line inputs, an audio recorder and sampling capabilities turn the Kross 2 into a live performance powerhouse. Load your own samples or capture audio on the fly--the possibilities for improvisation are endless.
Premium Keyboard Feel for Expressive Playing
The Kross 2 88-key model features Korg's lauded NH keybed, which recreates the weighted hammer action of an acoustic piano. Heavier in the lower register and lighter in the upper, the NH action allows for sensitive, nuanced playing across the full range of the keyboard. Piano and electric piano sounds truly come alive under your fingertips, while the keybed's portable design means you can bring the same premium feel to every performance.

3BR4242B200 Breakdown (Catalog Number)
This number defines the overall specifications for the panelboard as a complete unit.
3: Indicates 3-Phase power.
BR: Specifies the Breaker Type. This panel uses 1-inch "BR" style plug-on breakers.
42: The number of Spaces. This panel has 42 physical slots for breakers.
42: The number of Circuits. This means the panel is not designed for "twin" breakers; it supports 42 total circuits.
B: Indicates it is a Main Breaker unit (factory installed) rather than "Main Lug Only" (MLO).
200: The Amperage Rating. This unit is rated for 200 Amps.

title: Silver ginger kikiriki proven breeding pair
ai_notes: [Silver Kikiriki bantam breeding pair] Specialty breed of bantam chicken. Market is niche and local, making velocity slow.
description:
I am currently downsizing my birds and I'm offering for sale one of the first pairs I produced when I got into Kikiriki several years ago.
Please read in the ads entirety.
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
If you are unfamiliar with the breed Kiki are extremely small bantam birds originating in Puerto rico. They are extremely heat tolerant but absolutely not cold tolerant at all.
They MUST be brought inside during the winter. On the plus side they are very small birds and indoor rabbit hutches work for temporary winter housing in a pinch.
Everything in the world will want to eat them. Including small snakes, rats, and your house cat.  Careful thought needs to be put into predator-proofing your runs or cages.
They do best on bedding or ground. Wire is hard on Bird's feet and causes premature arthritis and breakdown of joint health. Think about it like working on concrete for 30 years as opposed to the plush office carpet
Because of the way they are built their center of gravity is not well balanced and they are prone to injury so be thoughtful with designs and keep purchase and climbing toys under several feet. I never trust their balance and try to refrain from having them on slick surfaces. Some birds do better than others but some of them are very clumsy.
Okay, on to the birds themselves.
This is Bridget and Cairo, they will be 3 years old in November. They are a proven pair of birds who have produced many chicks for me.
Because of the difference in their patterns they throw a handful of semi-predictable offspring colors. You can see some of those in examples in the photos included.
In addition to variations of Silver Ginger coloration these birds also carry a dilution Gene that produces what seems to be all female offspring in various brown/salmon versions of their normal offspring patterns. Thus far I have hatched no male chicks with this dilution obvious (though they can carry it), only females. It's a lovely variant.
In reference to their chicks, they produce short, mid-leg, and tall chicks as do most Kiki's. They also produce crested and bonehead chicks occasionally, and varied degrees of beards and muffs.
Both birds can be handled easily enough for treatments but do not care for affection or handling for fun. Agreeable but aloof. The male is protective and will peck or flog to correct or put space between you and them if he's uncomfortable. He is not aggressive. This is not a behavioral issue, it's personality. His chicks do not share his prickliness.
These birds have been allowed to raise several clutches of chicks. They are both good parents however the male becomes much more aggressively protective when there are chicks and will flog you, the mother does not like the disturbance and so often times tries to correct the male which leads to skirmishes between the parents. While both take care of the chicks and do well with them I generally take him away if I'm allowing her to raise chicks just so they don't have disagreements.
That being said parent raised chicks are always more feral and will require a lot more work than brooder raised chicks so I recommend raising them yourself.
The chicks that they have produced have been friendly and gregarious when raised by me. Chicks raised by them are aloof and require more time and patience but also can be very friendly.
These are not crossbred birds they are kikiriki, with genetics from a reputable person who has been in the hobby for many years, and is part of the community they were developed by.  They are not micro however so you will still have birds ranging between 12 oz and a little over a pound and at maturity despite a diminutive size (water bottle-ish).

Everything from Bald Eagles, elk, black bear and an occasional cougar have been spotted as well.

description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.

title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
ai_notes: [Antique UPRR train track level] Collectible railroad tool, price not specified.
description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.
Thanks
